
Conditioning for Poisson processes^[[_NOT FOR PUBLICATION_]{.mark}] {#sec-poisson}
==================================

The following example illustrates the need for precise and
careful specification when conditioning
on locations of points of Poisson point processes.

Consider a Poisson point process \(N\) of points in \((0,\Duration)\).

1. Condition on \(N\) placing at least one point in \((0,\Duration)\).
\[
\Prob{N(\Duration)=n\;|\; N(\Duration)>0}
\quad=\quad
\left(
\frac{\Duration^n}{n!} e^{-\Duration}
\right)/\left(1-e^{-\Duration}\right)
\quad=\quad
\frac{\Duration^n}{n!} \frac{e^{-\Duration}}{1-e^{-\Duration}}
\]
and so the conditional mean number of points in \((0,\Duration)\) is
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \; n \times \frac{\Duration^n}{n!} \frac{e^{-\Duration}}{1-e^{-\Duration}}
\quad=\quad
T \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\Duration^{n-1}}{(n-1)!} \frac{e^{-\Duration}}{1-e^{-\Duration}}
\quad=\quad
\frac{\Duration}{1-e^{-\Duration}}\,.
\]
Observe that as \(\Duration\to\infty\) so
\[
\frac{\Duration}{1-e^{-\Duration}} - \Duration \quad=\quad \Duration \frac{e^{-\Duration}}{1-e^{-\Duration}} \quad\to\quad0\,,
\]
while
\[
1+\Duration   - \frac{\Duration}{1-e^{-\Duration}} 
\quad=\quad 1 - \frac{\Duration e^{-\Duration}}{1-e^{-\Duration}}
\quad=\quad 1 - \frac{\Duration }{e^{\Duration}-1}
\quad>\quad 0\,.
\]

2. On the other hand we can apply the Slivnyak-Mecke theorem on the Palm distribution for a Poisson point process 
[@ChiuStoyanKendallMecke-2013, Example 4.3]; under Palm conditioning on there being a point at location \(t\in[0,\Duration)\),
the remaining assembly of points still has the distribution of \(N\)
(intuitively clear from the independence properties of a Poisson point process!).
Thus the (Palm)-conditional mean is \(1+\Duration\), strictly greater than the mean computed above.

The Slivnyak-Mecke approach is the one appropriate for our purposes, as we need to condition
on specific points (times of activated removals). This arises in the zero-width limit when we condition
on there being points in each of a fixed number of intervals of specified width.
